harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense) as router between lan-a (vtnet1/opt1, 10.60.10.0/24, peering node2's eth1) and lan-b (vtnet2/opt2, 10.60.20.0/24, peering node3's eth1). Added default-deny-overriding pass rules for both interfaces plus a directional hybrid-mode outbound SNAT rule (OPNsense/Firewall/Filter/snatrules) that translates lan-a→lan-b traffic to node1's lan-b address (10.60.20.1), while leaving lan-b→lan-a traffic untouched. Verified with live TCP connections: node2→node3 traffic arrives at node3 sourced from 10.60.20.1 (node1), while node3→node2 traffic arrives at node2 sourced from node3's own address (10.60.20.2), confirming the required asymmetric NAT behavior. Then performed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes (node2, node3, then node1/router), proving changed boot identity on each (Linux boot_id for node2/node3, FreeBSD kern.boottime for node1) and re-verifying full recovery of interface config, firewall/NAT rules, and the exact directional-NAT connection behavior after each restart.
actions_performed: Inspected topology: node1=OPNsense with vtnet0 (mgmt/lan), vtnet1 & vtnet2 unconfigured; node2/node3 have eth0 (mgmt, shared /24) and eth1 (unconfigured, links to node1)
Added OPT1 (vtnet1, LANA, 10.60.10.1/24) and OPT2 (vtnet2, LANB, 10.60.20.1/24) interfaces to node1 config.xml, applied via configctl interface reconfigure
Configured static IPs on node2 eth1 (10.60.10.2/24) and node3 eth1 (10.60.20.2/24) via nmcli (raw `ip addr add` was reverted by NetworkManager), plus static routes to the peer lan via node1
Added firewall pass rules for opt1 and opt2 in legacy <filter> section, applied via configctl filter reload; opened firewalld ports 5000/5001 (permanent) on node3/node2 for test listeners
Established TCP baseline (no NAT) confirming both directions show real source IPs

Added OPNsense SNAT rule under OPNsense/Firewall/Filter/snatrules (interface=opt2, source_net=opt1, target=10.60.20.1); corrected an initial mistake where the rule was placed under legacy <nat><rule> (became a DNAT/rdr rule) by moving it to the proper snatrules model, then reloaded filter
Verified directional NAT with live TCP connections both ways

Captured baseline boot markers (kern.boottime on node1, boot_id on node2/node3) and confirmed persisted config (interfaces, NAT mode, snatrules count) in config.xml, plus saved NetworkManager connection profile files
Restarted node2 via systemctl reboot (backgrounded ack), polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, restored listener, reverified NAT behavior both directions
Restarted node3 the same way, confirmed changed boot_id, restored listener, reverified NAT behavior both directions

Restarted node1 via /sbin/shutdown -r now (backgrounded ack), polled until reachable, confirmed changed kern.boottime, verified interfaces/pf NAT/filter rules auto-restored from config.xml, reverified end-to-end NAT behavior both directions

evidence.requirement: node2(lan-a)->node3(lan-b) connection observed by node3 as arriving from a chosen node1 address
evidence.summary: TCP connect from node2 to node3:5000 reported by node3's listener as originating from ('10.60.20.1', ...) -- node1's lan-b interface address, not node2's real address

evidence.requirement: node3(lan-b)->node2(lan-a) connection keeps its original source (no NAT applied in reverse direction)
evidence.summary: TCP connect from node3 to node2:5001 reported by node2's listener as originating from ('10.60.20.2', ...) -- node3's own real address, unmodified

evidence.requirement: Directional NAT rule correctly installed in pf / config.xml (not accidentally a port-forward)
evidence.summary: pfctl -s nat shows 'nat on vtnet2 inet from (vtnet1:network) to any -> 10.60.20.1 port 1024:65535' -- outbound SNAT only for lan-a-sourced traffic exiting via lan-b interface

evidence.requirement: Baseline (pre-restart) health of node1 router config and forwarding
evidence.summary: kern.boottime baseline captured (Sep 5 16:24:16 2026); config.xml confirmed to contain opt1/opt2 interfaces, hybrid NAT mode, 1 snatrules entry

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: boot identity change and post-restart recovery
evidence.summary: boot_id changed from 9bdcc129... to c6fe83df... after systemctl reboot; eth1 static IP/route and firewalld port persisted; live NAT test post-reboot confirmed correct asymmetric behavior in both directions

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: boot identity change and post-restart recovery
evidence.summary: boot_id changed from f54d7366... to c182563a... after systemctl reboot; eth1 config and firewalld port persisted; live NAT test post-reboot confirmed correct asymmetric behavior in both directions

evidence.requirement: node1 (router) restart: boot identity change and post-restart recovery of routing/firewall/NAT and full data-plane behavior
evidence.summary: kern.boottime changed from 16:24:16 to 16:30:25 after /sbin/shutdown -r now; post-reboot pfctl confirmed opt1/opt2 interfaces, pass rules, and the directional SNAT rule auto-restored from persisted config.xml; live end-to-end TCP test post-reboot reconfirmed node2->node3 NATted to 10.60.20.1 and node3->node2 unmodified
